rationale: B wins because it finds the sharper reporter-shaped tension A leaves on the table: "Can you trust shopping advice from an AI that gets paid when you buy?" That is a real accountability angle, not just another monetization wrapper. A is disciplined and clean, but "One AI app, two new ways to take a cut" is the safer business-model synthesis; useful, but less likely to make an editor sit up.
gaps_in_A: Missed the consumer/accountability conflict hiding in the shopping launch: if Perplexity earns referral fees, ranking and recommendation neutrality become the uncomfortable story.
"One AI app, two new ways to take a cut" is distinct enough, but it overlaps with the first two angles and reads more like a synthesis than a fresh reporting lane.

The refused line "The publisher-payout angle: how much will publishers actually earn?" is too aggressively killed; payout opacity could be a reporting hook if paired with named publisher participation, not only proof-it-needs.
gaps_in_B: "after months of legal threats" invents duration. The update says Perplexity has faced criticism and legal threats, not that the threats lasted months.

"the kind who has already written about publishers' criticism and legal threats against Perplexity" assumes prior coverage by the target reporter. Keep it as a beat descriptor, not a guessed byline history.

"how a multi-billion-dollar AI company plans to pay for itself" leans on valuation language a little too hard without revenue figures; B catches this in proof, but the headline still risks investor-thesis overreach.
